catalog_quote: 4.2 PWB phonological word. Most WB languages are sesquisyllabic-a word may consist of one or one and a half syllables. In the latter case a stressed mainsyllable is preceded by a minorsyllable, a structurally impoverished unit that is constructed from a restricted set of segments. The minorsyllable typically consists of an oral stop or fricative of unmarked phonation type, an epenthetic ([a] or schwa-like) vowel, and may be closed by a nasal or rhotic. [p.33] ... Sesquisyllabism is typical for Bahnaric (and many other MK languages), and therefore it seems reasonable to assume it for PWB. ... This leads us to suppose that the phonological word in PWB was restricted to the following possibilities: Type 1: C(R)V(F) Type 2: Cə.RV(F) Type 3: C(r/n).CV(F) [p.34] ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (minor syllable + main syllable); stress falls on the main syllable, which is word-final. The Lavi profile (pp.11-13) analyses Lavi words into minorsyllable onsets (p t c k ʔ m r l s j h, vowel [a]/[i]) plus a full mainsyllable, and L-Thongkum's own Lawi transcriptions (MKS 27, 1997; PL-530, 2002) mark stress before the final syllable (pa'tor 'star', ta'pit 'ear', sa'nAAm 'house'), consistent with final (main-syllable) stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. Sidwell & Jacq note Lavi minorsyllables may carry aspirated onsets and [i] vowels (secondary, from infixation/assimilation) and that L-Thongkum often writes a minorsyllable vowel for Lavi where it is not phonemic (p.49); no statement that any word type has non-final stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is branch-level ('Most WB languages'), made by authors with first-hand Lavi fieldwork (Sidwell 2002 recordings) in a handbook whose Lavi chapter applies the main-/minor-syllable analysis to Lavi; domain is the phonological word (citation forms). The Lavi-specific prose phonology is in L-Thongkum 2001 (Thai), not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Sources call the language Lavi (Sidwell & Jacq 2003; ISO lvi) = Lawi (L-Thongkum 1997) = Savoeng/s@lwEN (autonym); all data are from Ban Lavi (Ban Fandeng/Phang Daeng), Lamam district, Sekong province -- the single moribund community, Glottolog lawi1235. The quoted stress sentence is a West-Bahnaric-wide statement (PL-551 sec. 4.2), applied to Lavi via the handbook's Lavi profile; the Lavi-specific primary phonology (L-Thongkum 2001, in Thai) was not accessible.

sources.note: Sec. 4.2 'PWB phonological word' p.33: most WB languages are sesquisyllabic; in a sesquisyllable 'a stressed mainsyllable is preceded by a minorsyllable' (i.e. stress on the word-final main syllable). Sec. 3.1 Lavi pp.11-13 gives Lavi mainsyllable/minorsyllable consonant and vowel inventories (from L-Thongkum 2001:399-401), notes devoicing + diphthongisation, minorsyllable vowels [a]/[i]; no separate Lavi-specific stress sentence.
